pr.title: Count the verdicts of reviews earlier releases published
pr.head: 5eeb454c034bf60b47693408c73b4feb96a362df

summary: Every Projector review ends its signature with a hidden HTML comment, the review marker, which records the verdict, the head commit it judged, the model that wrote it, and since release 0.6.10 the Projector version, as projector=. Several parts of Projector read a head's verdict back from that marker: the site's review status, project review status, and project review publish when it sets draft state or dismisses change requests.

Those readers share one strict pattern, MARKER, which required projector=. Reviews published by 0.6.9 and earlier have no such field, so they parsed as no verdict at all, and a pull request whose newest review predates 0.6.10 read as unreviewed. Reviews from 0.6.0 and earlier also spell a clean verdict approved, which the pattern rejected too.

This change makes projector= optional and accepts approved. verdict_marker, the one function that applies the pattern, reports approved as clean, so every reader sees one vocabulary. What publish writes does not change.
Projector's own review of this head found it clean, with no finding threads.

cards.title: Who reads the marker
cards.html:
• Site status: review_statuses in src/projector/site/__init__.py.
  • Status and draft state: newest_verdicts, used by project review status and by publish.
  • Dismissal: standing_change_requests, which decides which change requests count as Projector's.
  • Start comments: is_live, which treats a start comment as finished once its model has a verdict on that head.
  • Incremental rule: the only reader of the version, through Verdict.projector.

The collision check uses its own loose match on sha= and is unaffected.

groups.title: Reading older markers
groups.kicker: The marker pattern accepts the shapes earlier releases wrote
intro: All the change's behavior sits in src/projector/review.py. The MARKER regular expression now makes the projector= field optional and accepts verdict=approved. verdict_marker, which turns a review body into a Verdict record, maps approved to clean, so no caller ever sees the old word.

Verdict.projector, the version the marker names, becomes optional. Its one reader is the incremental-review rule. An incremental review is the short verdict a review loop posts on a small push, and it may build only on a full review made by this run's Projector version, model, and effort. A full review whose marker names no version still fails that rule. producer now names the missing version unknown in the refusal, where before the rule refused because the marker did not parse.

checks.text: Each release tag's marker template, from v0.5.0 through v0.6.10, keeps the field order the new pattern expects: verdict, optional projector, model, optional effort, then sha, findings, seconds, and covered. Checked with git grep at each tag.

files.note: The pattern, the Verdict type, the parser, and the refusal text the incremental rule prints.

checks.text: A marker with an empty projector=, a seven-character SHA, or no model= still fails to parse. Publish's self-check on the marker it writes therefore still refuses an empty version. Checked by running verdict_marker on each shape and by the new test_a_marker_still_needs_its_verdict_model_and_head.
Mapping approved to clean here, rather than in each reader, is what keeps the site, status, and dismissal code unchanged: each of them compares the verdict against clean or changes-requested only.

Only the incremental rule calls producer with a marker's version. The other call passes this run's version from distribution_version, which is always a string and is itself unknown when no installed release is found.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: One test per reader, plus the parser itself
intro: Each reader the bug affected gets a test that strips projector= from a fixture's marker, and where it matters rewrites clean as approved. The site's fixture helper projector_review gains a version argument so a test can write a marker with no version.
The site test also parses a verbatim marker copied from a real pre-0.6.10 review, so the fixture shape is not the only evidence.

checks.text: With the head's tests run against the base's review.py, the four new behavior tests fail: dismissal, status, the interdiff rule, and site status. So a test cannot pass because its replace call matched nothing. With the head's code, the full suite runs 842 tests and passes, with one expected skip.

files.note: Parser tests in VerdictMarkerTests, and one test each for dismissal, status, and the incremental rule.

checks.text: The status test rewrites both fixtures. Only the newest, clean one is affected by the approved rewrite, and it is the verdict the test asserts.

files.note: A site status test for older markers, and a version argument on the projector_review fixture helper.
